record.original_question: What is the minimal possible length of a space curve that is visible from every point of a given sphere?

evidence.quote: Une variante du problème, posée par ALAIN GRIGIS, et déjà signalée dans [3], est comme suit : Quelle est la longueur minimale d’une courbe de l’espace qui peut être vue de tout point de la sphère ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the unit sphere, viewed as an opaque body: a point $p \in S$ "sees" a point $q \in \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (where $B$ is the closed unit ball bounded by $S$) if the open line segment from $p$ to $q$ does not intersect the interior of $B$. Equivalently, $q$ is visible from $p$ if and only if $q$ lies in the closed half-space $H_p = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \langle x - p, p\rangle \ge 0\}$ tangent to $S$ at $p$.

A rectifiable curve $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B)$ (not assumed closed and not assumed connected to anything) is said to be visible from every point of the sphere if for every $p \in S$ there exists a point $q \in \gamma$ with $q \in H_p$, i.e. $\gamma \cap H_p \neq \emptyset$.

Determine
$$
L^* \;=\; \inf \bigl\{\, \mathrm{length}(\gamma) \;:\; \gamma \text{ is a rectifiable curve in } \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \mathrm{int}(B) \text{ visible from every point of } S \,\bigr\},
$$
and exhibit (or characterize) a curve attaining this infimum, if one exists.
artifact.status_search_result: For closed inspection curves the analogous problem was settled by Ghomi and Wenk (Crelle 2021), who proved that any closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose convex hull contains the unit sphere has length at least $4\pi$, with equality for a baseball-seam-shaped union of four semicircles (Zalgaller's conjecture). The version for arbitrary (not necessarily closed) space curves visible from every point of the sphere does not appear to be resolved in this literature; no published proof of an exact minimum or characterization of an extremal curve for the open-curve variant was found.

status_evidence.title: Shortest closed curve to inspect a sphere (Ghomi–Wenk)
status_evidence.snippet: Any closed curve which lies outside the unit sphere and contains the sphere within its convex hull has length at least 4π, with equality for a baseball-seam curve.
status_evidence.claim: The closed-curve version of the sphere-inspection problem is solved with optimal length 4π.

status_evidence.title: Shortest closed curve to contain a sphere in its convex hull
status_evidence.snippet: Generalization showing closed curves with the unit sphere in their convex hull have length ≥ 4π, with characterization of equality.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work also addresses only the closed-curve case, not arbitrary space curves.
